title: iPad (11th gen) won't power on: diagnose and fix
diagnosis: A completely dead iPad is most often a drained battery, a faulty cable or charger, or dirt in the USB-C port. I'll walk you through the no-tools checks first, then the port cleaning, which fixes most cases.
safety_notes: Never open the iPad if it is swollen, hot or the screen is lifting; stop and take it to a repair shop.
Do not use metal tools or liquids inside the USB-C port.

steps.title: Unplug and remove accessories
steps.instruction: Disconnect everything from the iPad and take it out of any keyboard case. Place it on a clear table.
steps.expected_visual_state: The iPad lies alone on the table with no cables, case or keyboard attached.
common_mistakes: Leaving the keyboard case on, which hides the Smart Connector
Troubleshooting with a damaged cable still attached

steps.title: Check the USB-C port for lint
steps.instruction: Shine a flashlight into the USB-C port. Gently scrape out any lint with a wooden toothpick or plastic spudger.
steps.expected_visual_state: The USB-C port shows a clean, empty slot with the tongue visible and no lint packed in.
common_mistakes: Using a metal pin that can short the contacts
Pushing lint deeper instead of scooping it out

steps.title: Connect a known-good charger
steps.instruction: Plug a known-good cable into a wall charger of 20W or more, then into the iPad. Use a different outlet from any you suspect.
steps.expected_visual_state: The iPad is connected by cable to a wall charger that is plugged into a wall outlet.
common_mistakes: Charging from a laptop USB port, which may be too weak
Using a frayed or non-certified cable
Not pushing the plug fully into the port

steps.title: Charge for at least 30 minutes
steps.instruction: Leave the iPad plugged in untouched for 30 minutes. A deeply drained battery needs time before the screen reacts.
steps.expected_visual_state: The iPad is still plugged in, and the screen may show the charging battery or Apple logo.
common_mistakes: Giving up after a few minutes

steps.title: Force restart
steps.instruction: While still plugged in, press and release volume up, then volume down. Then hold the top button for 10 seconds or until the Apple logo appears.
steps.expected_visual_state: The screen lights up and the Apple logo appears.
common_mistakes: Pressing the buttons in the wrong order
Releasing the top button too early

steps.title: Try another cable and charger
steps.instruction: If the screen is still black, swap in a different cable and charger and wait 15 more minutes. Then repeat the force restart.
steps.expected_visual_state: A different cable and charger are plugged into the iPad, and the screen is either on or still black.
common_mistakes: Changing only the cable but not the charger
Not repeating the force restart after swapping

steps.title: Confirm the fix
steps.instruction: Unplug the iPad and hold the top button to power it on. Check that it boots and charges normally.
steps.expected_visual_state: The iPad shows the Apple logo, reaches the lock screen and shows a charging icon when plugged in.
common_mistakes: Assuming it is fixed without testing on battery
Ignoring a screen that stays black, which means a service visit for the battery or logic board
